attach smd: a via or trace connection anchored to the center of a surface-mount pad
autorouter: the batch automatic routing engine that connects nets with traces and vias
bend cost: router penalty added when a trace changes direction on a layer
board outline: the PCB edge boundary; copper and keepouts must stay inside it
clearance: the minimum allowed distance between two copper or mechanical features
clearance class: a named group of spacing rules applied to traces, vias, and areas
clearance matrix: table defining clearance values between item classes on a layer
clearance violation: a design-rule failure where two items are closer than allowed
component: a placed footprint instance on the board
component keepout: a zone where components must not be placed (place keepout)
conduction area: a filled copper region tied to one net (pour/plane); Freerouting term
courtyard: the minimum keepout boundary around a component body
DSN: Specctra design file (.dsn) exchanged with KiCad, EAGLE, and similar EDA tools
fab: fabrication layer showing component body outlines for assembly drawings
fanout: short traces and vias from dense pads (e.g. BGA) to escape routing layers
gate: Specctra term for a logical grouping of pins within a component
gate pin: a pin referenced through a component gate in Specctra format
keepout: a zone where traces, vias, or placement are forbidden
layer: a PCB copper, mask, silkscreen, or documentation plane
logical part: Specctra term for a component definition before placement
neckdown: automatic trace width reduction where the route enters a narrower pad
net: an electrical connection grouping all pins that must be connected
net class: a set of routing rules (trace width, via rule, clearance) shared by nets
obstacle area: a copper or mechanical area that blocks or restricts routing
optimizer: post-routing pass that shortens and cleans up existing traces
package: Specctra term for a footprint definition (land pattern)
padstack: the pad + drill hole pattern defining a pin or via on each layer
pin: a component terminal that must be connected by copper
power plane: a copper pour layer used for power or ground distribution
preferred direction: horizontal or vertical routing bias configured per signal layer
pull tight: interactive operation that straightens and optimizes trace geometry
push and shove: interactive routing mode that pushes existing traces aside (shove)
ratsnest: temporary lines showing unrouted connections between pads
ripup: remove existing trace segments so a net can be rerouted
SES: Specctra session file (.ses) containing routing results for import
shove fixed: net attribute: trace cannot be displaced by push/shove routing
signal layer: a copper layer used for trace routing (not plane-only)
silkscreen: legend layer for component reference designators and markings
SMD: surface-mount device pad (not a through-hole pin)
Specctra: PCB interchange format (also called Electra DSN) used by Freerouting
stitch mode: routing mode used for shove-fixed nets that must stay in place
terminal item: a connectable board item at the end of a route (pin, via, area)
trace: a copper track connecting pads, vias, or areas on one layer
trace length: the routed length of a copper segment
trace width: the width of a copper trace
unroute: remove routing from selected items or nets
unrouted: not yet connected by finished copper routing
via: a plated hole connecting traces on different layers
via keepout: a zone where vias are not allowed
via rule: defines which via padstacks and layer spans a net class may use
